data.one_liner: Flutter plugin that streams ambient light sensor (lux) values on Android and iOS.
data.what_it_does: Exposes a native ambient light sensor reading as a Dart stream of integer lux values. Handles iOS SensorKit entitlement and permission requests, while Android works without extra permissions.
use_when: You need real‑time ambient light data for adaptive UI or research purposes
Your app runs on devices that support the ambient light sensor and you can obtain the required iOS entitlements
avoid_when: You cannot obtain the required SensorKit entitlement on iOS
Target devices lack an ambient light sensor
You only need a simple brightness level without sensor precision
strengths: Simple API with a single stream
Supports both Android and iOS natively
weaknesses: iOS requires special entitlement and setup, making it hard for many apps
Limited to devices that expose an ambient light sensor
Only provides raw lux integers, no higher‑level processing
data.setup_notes: On iOS add the SensorKit entitlement (com.apple.developer.sensorkit.reader.allow) with ambient-light-sensor, include NSSensorKitUsageDetail in Info.plist, and request authorization via Light().requestAuthorization(). Android needs no extra permissions.

alternatives.name: sensors_plus
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides access to a wide range of device sensors without special iOS entitlements, useful if you need other sensors or want a simpler setup.
